title: Gabby Windey Conquered Reality TV. Now She’s Determined to Be Your New Favorite Actress
full_text: × Skip to main content Gabby Windey ventures into the scripted world of television with 'The Body.' Photography Courtesy “Teenagers really terrify me,” jokes Gabby Windey . Ironic for an actor in TV’s latest high-school set ensemble show. The former ICU nurse and NFL cheerleader turned TV personality rose to pop culture stardom on The Bachelor and co-led her own season of The Bachelorette . In the time since, she won the internet’s favorite competition series, The Traitors , and did a stint on Dancing With the Stars , placing second in her season. Now, she’s diving headfirst into a career in acting with The Body . “Reality’s dead to me,” Windey says, cheekily. It’s a joke, but there’s likely an inkling of truth there. The 35-year-old is intent on building a career as an actress. Related Stories TV 'Virgin River' Renewed for Netflix-Record Ninth Season Movies 'Heartland' Review: Jessica Chastain Does Sturdy Work as a Hard-Edged Former Country Music Star Saddled With a Thriller in Name Only She’s grateful for the experiences she’s had on TV leading up to this point, but she’s not sure there’s anything left for her in that space. “I loved all of my experiences,” she says. “I’m very aware it got me here, but just like everything, you want to grow and evolve. This is just the next step in my career.” Thankfully, she’s had some guidance in navigating the world. Windey, who publicly came out as a lesbian in 2023, has her wife, comedian and Hacks star Robby Hoffman, to help with practicing her lines and getting ready for her recent gigs. “I take work really seriously,” she says. Windey plays Coach Shauna Miller in Netflix ‘s coming-of-age genre-bending offering The Body . She auditioned for creator Quinn Shepard, who has said she felt inspired by the films she loved growing up when making the queer Catholic school thriller. “She’s gay, I’m gay, so I guess that’s all you need,” Windey jokes of why Shepard cast her. The actress was drawn to the show’s “dark” nature and the fact she, a former professional dancer, wasn’t playing a dancer. Instead, she plays the quirky, pregnant dance team coach. Below, Windey digs into The Body , her latest craft obsession and how that relates to the book she’s writing. We spoke very briefly after you won The Traitors . Hope you eventually got that prize money because at the time you were really concerned about them not paying you that . You know what? I did finally get it, but it’s like after I kicked and screamed. Classic. Well, you’re on The Body now. I was a little surprised to see you. How did this come about for you? I had auditioned for a couple roles before, just self-tapes, which are a scam we’re all learning. Nobody ever gets a job off of a self-tape. Quinn was my first Zoom, and I was terrified. It was so hot in my office. It was in the middle of last summer, so I was beat red, sweating, freaking out, and somehow still got the part. To anybody who’s nervous or feels like they blew it due to extreme heat, you’re fine. You can do it. Keep going. Where did you find inspiration for your role as the coach? Are there any iconic coaches of TV or movie past that you were getting inspired from? Not really. I know the coach from Glee , yes, is iconic, but no. I’ve had coaches before, but I mostly just thought — how would I be really as a coach? I’m not always surrounded by younger women. Teenagers really terrify me. They’re the scariest people in the world. Going to Sephora at 3 p.m. is my nightmare. I was just like, this is new for me, something I’m not around, so how would I be in a leadership role, which is very unserious? I think it checked out. Whether the coach was designed to be like this, or I was able to make it — what felt right to me just worked out because it turned out they don’t really need a coach. She’s kind of useless. What made you want to get into acting? Did you always have this aspiration or is it a more recent thing? I mean, it’s embarrassing to say out loud, “I want to be an actress,” so I never really did say it out loud. But I was hoping always a time would come. Getting onto TV, initially, I knew I wanted to make a career out of it. I didn’t know how or what that was going to look like. But once I signed with a bigger team and agents and stuff and I wanted to try it all. When I saw there was an acting agent in the room, I was like, oh, fuck yeah. If other people think I can do it, then I know I can do it. That just gives me an air of confidence, to have the resources. I’m auditioning. I’m not playing myself. I want to do roles. What was your experience like working with the cast on The Body ? I loved the cast, and I got really close with the girls. They’re all so talented and amazing. I’m in there with the Gen Z. They very much were like, “Oh, Millennial Gabby.” And I’m like, “Can you guys knock it off? I am the coolest millennial you will ever meet.” They were like, “Oh, it’s so nice seeing an older lesbian.” I’m like, “I’m literally going to kill you.” Murder-suicide. “I’m going to kill you first and then I’m going to kill myself.” They all meant it out of love. Not that I ever want to be inspiring or a role model to anybody, but some of the cast was queer, so I think it was nice seeing somebody like me who just is doing it and very happy. Obviously the acting is working out. You’re continuing to book roles. You also filmed Peaked recently. How was that? It was amazing. It was probably the best job I’ll ever have. I know it’s downhill from here. It was like summer camp. It’s a comedy. I was around some of the funniest people, so we just literally laughed all day. Molly Gordon is incredible. I cannot say enough about her. She just literally let me do what I wanted with the role too, which is amazing. There’s a lot of freedom. She trusted everybody. It was literally just play. My character in Peaked is who I’ve always wanted to be if I had no reservations. What roles are you hoping come your way? I’ve always wanted to be a scream queen. I’ve been screaming, screaming about the scream queen since the beginning. For some reason, it just hasn’t happened yet, but I think it would be really fun to play the victim and be a scared damsel. I told my agents that I don’t want to be pigeonholed in anything from the beginning of my career. I never wanted to be just one thing. I don’t just want to be the side comedy bitch. But with that being said, sets are way more fun when you’re laughing and you get to see everybody else in their prime. It’s like, do I want to enjoy my work or not? I don’t know if I would enjoy a drama, but you never know unless you try. What does your ideal day off look like? If you know that nothing is happening that day, what are you doing? God, I love a day off. I’m always in a nightgown, preferably 100 percent silk, back when clothes were good. Maybe it’s pink and a little mesh. Also, a silk robe and maybe some skincare. I’ll have my morning coffee and read a book. I’ll get high around 3 p.m., maybe craft a little and watch a good movie. My wife is right next to me, preferably saying nothing, which is very, very rare. It never happens, but you said an ideal day. Maybe ending [the day] with a good meal and good conversation, but not leaving the house. I will not leave the house on an ideal day. Do you need a bed-rot day every once in a while? Yes. Even just vacuuming. I like to be connected to the house, and vacuuming makes me feel connected emotionally. There’s nothing like a rug that’s freshly vacuumed. I don’t even know if Robby knows where the vacuum is, but she knows when it’s done, that’s for sure. I have houseplants, so I like to water the plants and prune them. Really… I’m a bit domesticated. It might surprise people. It surprises me, definitely, coming into my older self, but I’m growing mint. I don’t cook. It’s mostly for my friend, but it smells nice. I like to grow things. What’s your go-to craft at the moment? Everyone’s heard that I’m making pill bottles because everyone knows I’m ragingly depressed. I depend on medication. I have a sparkly pill bottle that I’ll take my day meds in my purse if I’m going to be gone, because I have to take meds three times a day. I’ve been wanting to make pill bottles, so I got little charms. Really, it’s just a distraction. I’m supposed to be writing a book, so I’m really needing to put it away. But this is taking up all my time. They take three hours to make. That’s kind of nice though. You can turn everything off. It’s so fun. They’re fun to look at. Everyone in my life is so sick of me talking about them because it’s all I want to talk about. I’ll ask if they want to see my pill bottles, [and they say] no. Well, too bad. THR

title: How to Become (and Stay) a Movie Star in 2026
full_text: × Skip to main content By Mia Galuppo Plus Icon Mia Galuppo Senior Entertainment Reporter miagaluppo Follow Sign Up View All November 13, 2026 7:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Stephen Kayln and Belmont Cameli in Off Campus, Sophie Neliesse and Hudson Williams in Heated Rivalry, Lola Tung in The Summer I Turned Pretty and Inde Navarette in Obsession Sabrina Lantos/HBO Max (2); Eddy Chen/Prime; Liane Hentscher/Prime (2); Focus Features One of Hollywood’s favorite subjects to pontificate on over business lunches — landing somewhere between the latest layoffs and who should really be cast as the next James Bond — is the state of the movie star. Where to find them? How to make them? Do they even still matter? In our annual Next Gen issue — which celebrates the future leaders of the entertainment industry, offscreen and on — The Hollywood Reporter has been doing our part to answer these questions, identifying a new crop of stars yearly. To compile this list , we trust our own instincts, certainly, but also survey executives, creatives and producers about the talent who excites them. This is how we tapped Sydney Sweeney well before her Euphoria fame and Glen Powell years ahead of his Top Gun ascent. More recently, we featured David Jonsson, who this summer stood on the Comic-Con stage taking on the mantle of Black Panther . Since the beginning of the industry itself, Hollywood has always relied on a steady stream of youthful stars to put in front of the entertainment-imbibing masses, from Clara Bow to James Dean to the Brat Pack. The talent both dictated and fulfilled the needs of the current moment. While Hollywood continues to slash content spends and M&A is laying waste to legacy studios, a potent combination of market forces and audience interests is working in favor of a certain type of young star. Despite all the turmoil, 2026 is actually a pretty good time to be an upwardly mobile talent. Call it entertainment’s very own K-curve. But young stardom is achieved in 2026 in a much different way than even 10 years ago. In the late 2010s, IP begot stars, as was the case with Spider-Man initially catapulting the careers of Tom Holland and Zendaya in 2017. There was also a well-worn path where an auteur director could tap a talent, and then the film festival and awards circuit would cement their status, as was the case with Timothée Chalamet in Luca Guadagnino’s Call Me by Your Name . Then there was the prestige TV contingent. Anya Taylor-Joy had worked steadily in indie movies but only landed at the top of studio wish lists following the success of Netflix’s The Queen’s Gambit , while Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones had Hulu’s much-watched Normal People to thank for their rise. As of late, a new class of stars has emerged, fully formed and ready for domination, from the recent spate of young adult series. Shows like The Summer I Turned Pretty , Sterling Point and Off Campus engendered fervent fan bases, building audiences for their leads seemingly overnight and creating immediate industry appeal for stars like Lola Tung and Stephen Kalyn, both a part of the Next Gen class of 2026. And while it may be difficult to remember a time before the omnipresence of Heated Rivalry , it has only been a year since that hockey show debuted, and leads Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams have leapfrogged to a level of fame that yields appearances everywhere from the Golden Globes to the Winter Olympics to a Monopoly Board. As for film, Gen Z is readily responding to the siren call of Nicole Kidman and her pinstripe pantsuit. In the past year, zoomers became the most active moviegoing age demographic. It is a direct rebuke of the once-prevailing wisdom of theatergoing: Let the kids stream and leave the cinema to the adults. In the spring, Inde Navarrette, the breakout from Obsession , proved that stardom can still happen the old-fashioned way, one popcorn bucket at a time. But once the fame has been achieved and the audience captured, the question quickly becomes: What’s next? Speaking to industry insiders working with and casting young talent, theatrical film is where these stars are advised to set their sights. To even the most skeptical in the industry, theatrical films best prove staying power and earning potential. While a lead role in a streaming feature can up a talent’s quote, it is better to take a smaller role and be farther down the call sheet — ideally under battle-tested A-listers — on a film that is supported by a robust studio marketing department with a healthy P&A spend. Talent must also now be extra cautious when signing on as the lead to a big-budget IP play. With superhero fatigue and interest among the sought-after Letterboxd generation in director-driven fare, a DC or Marvel lead is no longer a surefire king/queen maker, and not every toy-turned-tentpole is created equal (see: Supergirl and Masters of the Universe ). Young stars must show range. If you achieved success on a YA series, then a director-driven feature is a savvy next move. If you broke out in the latest hit horror, do not follow this with another thriller or else risk being pigeonholed by casting directors. At the same time, talent should not alienate those hard-won, recently amassed YA followings. For the stars of 2026, the majority of this audience is likely made up of women. Off Campus reached 36 million viewers worldwide in its first 12 days, according to Amazon, and is Prime Video’s most viewed series debut season of all time among the women 18-to-34 age demographic. After its finale, Warner Bros. Discovery said that Heated Rivalry earned 10.6 million U.S. viewers on HBO Max, with two-thirds of the audience being women. Unfortunately, theatrical slates are not geared toward female audiences. Romantic comedies are seen as the domain of streamers, and the evidently requisite annual Colleen Hoover adaptation doesn’t offer an abundance of employment opportunities. Still, Off Campus ‘ Belmont Cameli and Kalyn figured out a way to split the difference. Each will appear alongside the ever audience-conscious Sweeney in a studio film — Sony’s female-focused Sleepy Hollow adaptation from Barbie banner LuckyChap (Cameli) and Lionsgate’s sequel to The Housemaid (Kalyn). Then there are the entertainment extracurriculars. Fashion and luxury brands are quicker on the draw to tap young talent into campaigns — wanting to capitalize on zeitgeisty names with big social footprints — than in previous eras. In the short window since Storrie and Williams made their entrée into the collective public consciousness, Storrie landed a beauty contract with YSL and a jewelry ambassadorship with Tiffany & Co., while Williams fronted Balenciaga’s Summer 2026 campaign and was named a Bulgari brand ambassador. In the six months since Obsession ‘s May release and $500 million box office haul, Navarrette has become the face of Gap’s Fall 2026 collection and David Yurman’s holiday campaign. Plus, when you are making more money on a watch advertisement than you can expect from a paycheck on your sophomore feature, you can be choosier about where to place your time and talents. Just don’t wait too long. It’s often said that Hollywood has been relying on the same 12 names for the past two to five decades, give or take, to get audiences into theaters. But when Tom Cruise can’t open a movie, then even the most risk-averse executives are looking for some new talent. On our list, they’ll find plenty to choose from.

title: Stephanie Fuchs, Arianna Castoldi, Oscar Nominee Rémi Grellety Launch Autlook Collective, European Documentary Hub
full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew IDFA Artistic Director Isabel Arrate Fernandez On Festival’s Competition Lineups, “Huge” Interest In Elizabeth Holmes Doc, And AI In Documentaries Cinema Eye Honors Nominations: ‘American Doctor,’ ‘You Can See Everything’ Lead With 7; ‘Time And Water,’ ‘NAZA’ Close Behind [Full List] ‘The Baddest Speechwriter Of All’ Trailer: Ben Proudfoot And Stephen Curry Combine On Portrait Of Extraordinary Adviser To MLK View All November 13, 2026 6:41am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R Stephanie Fuchs, Arianna Castoldi, Rémi Grellety of Autlook Collective Severin Wurnig/Autlook Collective EXCLUSIVE: Three of documentary’s top talents are teaming up to form Autlook Collective , a new company conceived as a European documentary hub with expertise in sales and production. Stephanie Fuchs , CEO of Autlook Filmsales, Arianna Castoldi, former head of documentary at Mediawan Rights, and two-time Oscar-nominated producer Rémi Grellety , president of Warboys Films, are partnering on the forward-looking initiative that comes as many companies in the nonfiction space are scaling back. “The team’s role is to bring the right partners to the table at the right moment,” notes a release, “with a preference for joining projects during development or production, while there is still time to shape the financing plan and prepare the film’s launch.” Production involvement will be considered on a film-by-film basis, separately from sales representation. Related Stories Documentary IDFA Artistic Director Isabel Arrate Fernandez On Festival’s Competition Lineups, “Huge” Interest In Elizabeth Holmes Doc, And AI In Documentaries Documentary IDFA Announces Competition Lineups, Adds ‘Musk’ And Elizabeth Holmes Documentary ‘You Can See Everything’ “In these specific times and challenging ones, I think we should try things a bit differently,” Grellety tells Deadline. “I think there’s value in working together — producer and sales agent — earlier on in the life of a project. So, that means that we will have the ability on… a curated amount of projects, to come in early, try and find production money for the team, whether through French or European production, but also relying on our network of potential partners around the world, including in North America. And then be a part of the production and work with the team to launch the film in the best way possible — festival strategy, sales, awards campaign.” Watch on Deadline Autlook Filmsales is based in Vienna; Autlook Collective will be headquartered in Paris. “It was important for us to be a majority French company and not just a sub office or a new division,” comments Fuchs. “The idea is it’s going to be under the Autlook umbrella, so it will be [an] expansion, but also in order to start co-producing… it makes a lot of sense to do this in [Paris],” where Grellety is based. Castoldi will lead Autlook Collective’s sales activity, working closely with Fuchs and Autlook Filmsales. “The idea is obviously to keep on doing what Autlook is doing, but also be a key partner for both universes,” Castoldi says. “Meaning that if a French documentary producer needs our help for European partners and for partners outside Europe, we can do that. But at the same time, if an American partner or someone else coming from other parts of the world needs some help [getting] into Europe and into France, we can do it as well because we all have that experience. We all have behind us at least 10, 15 years of market experience. We know the people, we have already our network… Putting all our strengths together in a moment where the market is a little bit tough, we believe it’s the solution. So, expertise and know-how all together.” The Autlook Collective trio sees opportunity where others have shrunk to defensive positions. “It is risky to expand in a time where people are scaling down,” Fuchs acknowledges. “But… I strongly believe there has always been an audience for documentaries and it’s not going to go away… I think we’re in a very unique position that we have the strong standing or we have a strong slate and I’d much rather build on that and bank on that and risk the expansion rather than believing in the, let’s say, more negative outlook.” Adds Grellety, “Difficult times makes for daring choices. I think we have to be there. I think we all believe in documentaries… And even considering the state of the world, I think it’s even more important than ever.” Elizabeth Holmes in ‘You Can See Everything’ A24 /Courtesy Everett Collection The timing of the Autlook Collective launch, in fact, may be auspicious. Documentaries have enjoyed a sudden resurgence at the box office, led by the Elizabeth Holmes-themed film You Can See Everything , which has earned $80 million in the U.S. and is just beginning to open internationally, making $1.4 million abroad to date. NAZA , the investigative documentary about Israel’s conduct of the war in Gaza, has made $13.5 million internationally, against $1.3 million in the U.S. Everest: The Other Side , directed by Oscar winners Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin, has collected $1 million internationally and another $2 million domestically in less than two weeks of theatrical release. “When you see documentaries doing well at the box office again, and I feel like there is this new wind coming in, it’s also the perfect time [to launch],” notes Fuchs. “I believe that the audience is there, but maybe was a little bit waiting for something different in terms of stories,” Castoldi observes. “I would say the audience today is very attentive to the political situation all over the world. And the fact that some documentaries like Musk or like NAZA are bringing people to theaters, it’s a proof that there is an interest in the world around [us]; that has always been the core of documentaries.” Matthew Carey Autlook Collective will be a presence at the IDFA Forum, which runs Sunday through Wednesday (November 15-18) in Amsterdam. The new company isn’t ready to announce initial projects, but… “We are in discussions,” Fuchs allows. “I think for us all, it’s very important to not rush it and to not just sign films for the sake of signing them and starting with a big slate. It’s really the creation that’s important. But we have been starting to have conversations and starting to talk to filmmakers and to partners to also put the word out a bit like, ‘Look, that’s what we’re planning.’ Again, having the option to get on board earlier on that we currently have been doing also opens a lot more conversations that can happen.” Fuchs adds, “That’s why also IDFA’s going to be a very important moment for us to have these conversations in person when so many of, at least of the European doc community is going to be there.” Grellety will not only be representing Autlook Collective at IDFA, but the latest Oscar-contending film on which he serves as a producer, Closure , from director Michał Marczak, is also screening in the festival. His Oscar nominations came for producing I Am Not Your Negro and Soundtrack to a Coup d’Etat . The success of those documentaries speaks to a strong curatorial eye, an asset possessed by the three Autlook Collective principals. “We will build on what we know how to do, what we’ve been doing, which is a curated approach,” Grellety says of Autlook Collective. “A curated approach in selecting projects, in being there with the project over time and not just for a short moment of time. It’s this approach that is the core of what we want to do.” ‘Ebenezer’ At $1.5M In Previews; Johnny Depp Pic Seeks $40M WW Opening Jason Voorhees Returns: Steve Miner To Direct 13th Entry Of ‘Friday The 13th’ ‘Virgin River’ Gets Season 9 Renewal; Will Be Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series Outlook Email, Other Services “Approaching Normal” After Massive Outage Read More About: Comments

title: ‘Virgin River’ Gets Early Season 9 Renewal, Officially Becomes Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie NFL Quarterback Sam Hartman To Headline ‘The Bachelor’ For Season 30 On ABC ‘Virgin River’ Gets Early Season 9 Renewal, Officially Becomes Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series Hulu Series ‘The Spot’ Starring Claire Danes & Ewan McGregor Gets Release Date, First-Look Photos View All November 13, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L to R) Alexandra Breckenridge as Melinda Monroe and Martin Henderson as Jack Sheridan in Episode #701 of 'Virgin River' Courtesy of Netflix Netflix ‘s content leadership may be changing but one thing remains constant — Virgin River getting another early renewal. The long-running romantic drama starring Alexandra Breckenridge and Martin Henderson has been picked up for a ninth season months ahead of its 2027 Season 8 premiere. It will once again consist of 10 episodes, bringing the show’s total to 94 episodes. Patrick Sean Smith returns as showrunner and executive producer. With the renewal, Virgin River officially becomes the longest-running original scripted series on Netflix — and all of streaming — by number of seasons after taking the title with a qualifier last year. It has edged Spanish teen drama Elite , which ran for eight seasons. In number of episodes, 94, Virgin River ties current Netflix record holder, comedy Grace and Frankie, which produced seven seasons and is half-hour with an overall run time significantly shorter than that of hourlong Virgin River . Related Stories News 'The Body' Creators Address Show's "Unexplained Mysteries", Tease Season 2 Hopes Books Everything We Know About Netflix's 'Icebreaker' Adaptation So Far Alongside the renewal, Netflix also revealed that the adaptation of the popular Robyn Carr novels has passed the half-billion views mark this year. Watch on Deadline Virgin River, one of Netflix’s “blue sky”, “comfort” series, has defied the notion that streaming series cannot run for too long. The show has benefited from its sustainable premise, chronicling relationships among characters in a small town, appealing leads in Breckenridge and Henderson and strong supporting cast anchored by veterans Tim Matheson and Annette O’Toole, as well as attractive economics, keeping the budget reasonable by filming in Canada in a handful of primary locations with few stunts or special effects involved. The string of early renewals handed to Virgin River in the last few years has allowed the series to stay on a yearly cadence, dropping a new season every 11-13 months. There is no release date yet for Season 8 but a late spring premiere appears likely. As Deadline reported in March , Season 8 won’t feature two longtime cast members who are not returning, Marco Grazzini, who played Mike, and Lauren Hammersley, who portrayed Charmaine. Joining the cast is Natasha Calis in the heavily recurring role of Dr. Astrid, with an option to become a series regular in Season 9. Virgin River, which wrapped production on Season 8 in August, follows the romantic journey of nurse practitioner Melinda Monroe (Breckenridge), who moved to the remote California town of Virgin River after a personal tragedy, and charismatic local bartender Jack (Henderson), who is haunted by his past. The renewal comes a month after Peter Rice joined Netflix as new Chief Content Officer. It was done by Head of UCAN (US – Canada) Scripted Series Jinny Howe, who has continued in her role after the executive shake-up, now reporting to Rice. A self-professed romance buff, Howe was a fan of Virgin River before taking oversight of the show starting with Season 5 when Smith came in as new showrunner, replacing Sue Tenney. “Mel, Jack, and the whole town of Virgin River have become a place that feels like coming home, for viewers around the world,” Howe said. “Reaching Season 9 as our longest-running original scripted series, with over half a billion views, is a milestone that speaks to how deeply fans continue to love being a part of this community. Patrick Sean Smith and the entire team have done a beautiful job in keeping fans engaged in this world, and we can’t wait to invite fans back for more.” Season 8 will follow Mel and Jack’s journey as new parents as their adopted baby is fighting for his life. Across its first seven seasons, Virgin River has spent 28 weeks in the Global Top 10, and reached the Top 10 in over 80 countries. Smith executive produces with Erin Cardillo, Richard Keith, Jackson Sinder, Mary Page Keller, Thomas Ian Griffith, Norman Buckley, Ian Hay, Tenney, Roma Roth, Christopher E. title: ‘Project Hail Mary’ Cinematographer Greig Fraser On Bringing 1980s Pop Culture Influences To Ryan Gosling Sci-Fi Hit — ToruńCamerimage
full_text: Skip to main content By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana ‘Project Hail Mary’ Cinematographer Greig Fraser On Bringing 1980s Pop Culture Influences To Ryan Gosling Sci-Fi Hit — ToruńCamerimage From Local to Global: Anshuman Jha & Sarah-Jane Dias On Advocating Animal Rights In ‘Lakadbaggha 2’ & Uniqueness Of Crafting An Indian Action Franchise Rooted In Local Martial Arts Rising Star Molly McCann On Finding Her Place In Panem For ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ View All November 13, 2026 5:41am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ryan Gosling in 'Project Hail Mary' Amazon MGM Studios/Everett Collection Oscar-winning cinematographer Greig Fraser took time out of shooting Sam Mendes’ The Beatles films to reflect on how he and directors Phil Lord and Christopher Miller crafted the visuals for summer box office hit Project Hail Mary . Fraser spoke to Deadline during the Toruń Camerimage Film Festival and said that working with Lord and Miller had been a long time in the making. “I’ve known Phil and Christopher for a while in passing but we hadn’t worked together yet until this film,” he said. “What I love about them is that there is definitely a thread that runs through their films but genre-wise, they are completely different in everything they do. They are like these savants that just keep flicking between different formats and ratios and stories but there is an underlying theme in their work. What I think is beautiful about their work is that we all grew up on the same films and he same cartoons and we are all influenced by the same series of things.” Related Stories News 'Project Hail Mary' Composer Daniel Pemberton Built "A Language From The Ground Up" Using New Instruments - Sound & Screen Film Festivals Camerimage Opens With Minute Of Silence For Kraków Mass Shooting; Darren Aronofsky Honored & Luca Guadagnino Introduces 'Artificial' Fraser noted that pop culture references from the 1980s featured heavily in the discussions about how to portray the look of the Ryan Gosling starrer and he specifically noted Lord’s mention of Scooby-Doo when they discussed conveying the story’s transitions from space to Earth. Watch on Deadline “It gave me the idea in my head about the Scooby-Doo transition of the wobbly lines when there was a flashback,” he says. “I knew exactly what he was talking about. I also knew that in no way, shape or form would any film that we all contribute to have wobbly lines, and he said the same thing. So, then everything became a translation of how we do what we felt in the 1980s from films like E.T. or cartoons from pop culture. How do we translate that into what we’re creating now as filmmakers.” To achieve this look, Fraser, whose credits also include the first two instalments of Dune and The Batman , said he shot with a mis-timed shutter to create image streaking when transitioning the scenes. Project Hail Mary is an Amazon MGM film, which sees Ryan Gosling play a science teacher who wakes up in a spaceship light years away only to discover he is humanity’s sole hope to save Earth from a sun-dimming parasite. The film, which is based on Andy Weir’s novel of the same name, splits across two alternating timelines – present-day space and flashbacks on Earth. Fraser outlined the reasoning behind making the space scenes feel a “bit cooler” and the Earth scenes “a bit warmer.” “It was a fine balance to strike because you could absolutely go on a trope of space being cold and fluorescent lit and all kind of sci-fi,” he said. “And Earth is this thing that they are fighting for, and this is why he’s up there. So, you needed to be warm with the memories, and you need these things to be lovely memories. “But, at the same time, the Earth is dying because the sun is dying and you don’t want to sit through two and a half to three hours of a film where you want to jump off a building. You really need to come out and enjoy his experience, and he needs to grow from the experience.” The Australian DoP added that the opening scene, where Gosling’s character wakes up in space unaware of where he is, was crucial. “We specifically did not want that to feel like a space film,” he said. “He couldn’t wake up in a laboratory. I wanted him to wake up in a high-end hotel or what was effectively a high-end health retreat, so the audience is kind of discombobulated about where he is and what he is doing. He continues: “There’s a CG shot, which we all designed, where the camera goes past revealing him as this tiny person in this little window [in the spaceship] and this is another pop culture reference where we referenced The Empire Strikes Back as there’s a scene at the end of that film where you’ve got these little figures in the window. We liked that idea that he’s on a journey going past.” ToruńCamerimage takes place November 7-14, 2026. ‘Ebenezer’ At $1.5M In Previews; Johnny Depp Pic Seeks $40M WW Opening Jason Voorhees Returns: Steve Miner To Direct 13th Entry Of ‘Friday The 13th’ ‘Virgin River’ Gets Season 9 Renewal; Will Be Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series Microsoft Seeing “Improvements” As Outlook Email Comes Back Up Read More About: Comments

full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Microsoft Outlook Still Down In 365 Outage: Company Sees Sporadic Improvements, Though No Sustained Recovery CJ 4DPlex Pacts With B&B Theatres To Equip Single Missouri Site With 3 Premium Large Format Screens ‘Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope’ To Play At Cosm As Disney Teams With Shared Reality Firm View All November 12, 2026 8:53pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images UPDATED with latest company comments: Earlier this evening Microsoft posted an update on the outages to its 365 platform noting “positive results with our efforts to restart affected infrastructure and recover server availability.” The optimism was short lived. About an hour later, the company announced that their efforts were “not taking as expected.” The company subsequently said it was “adjusting traffic protocols, redistributing traffic, and applying strategic traffic blocking measures,” and “observing partial recovery across regions in which we’ve applied these adjustments.” The bad news was, it reported, “these actions aren’t resulting in sustained recovery.” Related Stories News Microsoft Offers Buyouts To 60,000, A Quarter Of Its Workforce News Eyeing More 'Minecrafts' And 'Fallouts', Microsoft Xbox Launches XP Unit To Take Properties Beyond Video Games The widespread outages began around 1 p.m. ET, and impacted users in the United States and elsewhere. Watch on Deadline The tech giant issued a string of social media posts throughout the day on Thursday acknowledging that users had been reporting issues with access, throwing a major wrench into business communications across sectors. Enterprise and business customers of Microsoft 365 were experiencing problems connecting to email via the Exchange server as well as accessing other services. The U.S. is one of the main regions affected, but Microsoft says it potentially poses a problem across the world. As the outage dragged into the end of the work day, the tech giant put out a less-than-encouraging status report. “We’re continuing to pursue all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” the company wrote. “Our investigation has found that a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss.” Workers are “fully isolating a portion of our service infrastructure, restarting the affected components, and gradually reintroducing traffic to confirm our services remain stable,” the company went on to say. “We’re also analyzing traffic patterns across our entire service infrastructure and evaluating whether isolating traffic within each region may allow affected regions to recover independently.” After the initial issues with email, word surfaced about users unable to connect with Teams, Azure, OneDrive, Copilot and other offerings. The home page of outage detection site DownDetector was filled almost entirely by Microsoft alerts. “We’re investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas,” the company posted at around noon ET on Thursday. “While we’re working to mitigate impact, we’ve confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region.” Microsoft later clarified, “We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” A status hub designed to provide service updates cited “an unexpected increase in a specific type of service traffic to determine whether it’s contributing to the elevated load. In parallel, we’re evaluating options to redirect traffic to alternate infrastructure to expedite relief.” Media companies were among those across all business sectors whose activities slowed to a crawl due to the tech glitch. Employees at Amazon Prime Video, Skydance and NBCUniversal and other companies confirmed to Deadline they were in the dark. There were no immediate indications of a possible cause, though online speculation touched on factors like digital downloads of Grand Theft Auto VI pre-orders or hackers looking to make a statement. Still other theories sought to connect the outage to the day’s other momentous tech news: the ouster of Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of Nvidia. Huang was forced to resign after admitting to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and amid reports of affairs with executives at his own company. The origins of Microsoft 365 date to the early 2010s, when the company was ramping up its efforts to transition its Office programs Word, Excel and PowerPoint to the cloud. After a meteoric rise as a software maker in the 1980s and 1990s, Microsoft weathered some lean years after a federal antitrust lawsuit and a sluggish initial response to the advent of the internet. Under CEO Satya Nadella, Microsoft has successfully pivoted into cloud computing and, more recently, AI en route to a multi-trillion-dollar market valuation. Shares in Microsoft have thus far not been affected by the outage, finishing Thursday’s trading day up a fraction to $523. The company’s stock, along with those of a dozen or more large companies placing heavy bets on AI, will come under increasing scrutiny on Wall Street in light of the Nvidia news.
